what: glm5.2-fp4-mi355x-sglang-agentic-mtp (TP4/EP4, HiCache): add SGLang flags --enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion and --enable-fused-qk-norm-rope, and export AITER_USE_FLYDSL_MOE_SORTING=1, in benchmarks/single_node/agentic/glm5.2_fp4_mi355x_sglang_mtp.sh.
mechanism: AR+RMSNorm fusion folds the TP all-reduce into the following RMSNorm (about 80 standalone collective kernels per forward removed); fused QK-norm+RoPE+KV-write does one kernel per attention layer instead of three; FlyDSL MoE token sorting replaces the default sorting kernel in MoE dispatch. All three kernels already ship in the image (v0.5.16-rocm720-mi35x-20260728); they match ATOM's default dispatch for GLM-5.2.
effect: +23.6% P90 E2E normalized interactivity (41.9 -> 51.8 tok/s/user) at CONC=8, TP4/EP4 HiCache, AgentX cc-traces.
why: Two of the three are documented SGLang server flags that a profile (many standalone all-reduce and norm/rope kernels at decode) points straight at. The AITER env var is undocumented in SGLang, but it is visible in the AITER source in the image and in ATOM's defaults; the commit is itself co-authored by an agent. Mild difficulty only in knowing that ATOM's dispatch is a reference to diff against.

Llama-3.3-70B FP8/FP4 B200 vLLM (70b_b200_slurm.sh): new squash image; pip-reinstall nvidia-nccl-cu12==2.26.2.post1 and build FlashInfer from commit 97201824; export VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_FUSION_THRESHOLDS_MB='{"2":32,"4":32,"8":8}'; compilation-config becomes pass_config{enable_fi_allreduce_fusion, enable_attn_fusion, enable_noop} + custom_ops [+quant_fp8,+rms_norm] + cudagraph_mode FULL_DECODE_ONLY + splitting_ops []; drop --quantization modelopt; --max-num-seqs 512 appended (overrides $CONC). Series: 19, 24 (FlashInfer 0.3.0 wheel replaces the source build, NCCL pin dropped), 25/26/28 (quoting fixes), 30 (docker runner).
mechanism: FlashInfer's fused all-reduce+RMSNorm(+FP8 quant) is used up to a per-world-size message size (raised to 32 MB at TP2/4, 8 MB at TP8) instead of NCCL all-reduce plus separate norm/quant kernels; attention fusion folds the FP8 output quant of the next GEMM into the attention kernel (needs +quant_fp8 exposed as a custom op so the pattern matcher sees it); FULL_DECODE_ONLY with no splitting ops captures the whole decode step, attention included, in one CUDA graph instead of piecewise graphs, removing per-layer launch gaps. The FlashInfer commit and NCCL 2.26 provide the fused kernels these passes call.
why: The compilation passes are documented vLLM options, but they only fire as a set: attn fusion needs +quant_fp8 visible, full decode graphs need splitting_ops emptied, and AR fusion needs a size threshold per TP; one-knob-at-a-time screening can see each alone as neutral or broken. The decisive part is outside the loop: it reinstalls NCCL and builds FlashInfer from an unreleased commit at launch, i.e. a library/image change the agent may not make and would only know to make by following FlashInfer/vLLM upstream. The threshold map covers TP2/4/8, so most of it pays off at points a single-TP campaign never measures.

DeepSeek-R1 FP8 B200 SGLang (TP8): image lmsysorg/sglang v0.4.10.post1 -> v0.5.0rc1-cu128-b200; SGLANG_ENABLE_FLASHINFER_GEMM=true; --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3; --stream-interval 1; drop --disable-shared-experts-fusion; cuda-graph-max-bs 256->128, max-running-requests 512->128, mem-fraction-static 0.89->0.82. Series: reverted by 22, re-landed by 23.
mechanism: FlashInfer's Blackwell FP8 block-scale GEMM replaces the default dense FP8 GEMM path; FP8 KV halves MLA KV bytes read per decode step and doubles cache capacity; re-enabling shared-experts fusion folds the shared expert into the routed MoE kernel (one grouped GEMM instead of two); smaller graph/running caps match the swept concurrencies and free memory for FP8 KV.
why: The flags exist only in the newer SGLang image, which the loop cannot change; the env var SGLANG_ENABLE_FLASHINFER_GEMM is not in --help, it is read in SGLang's FP8 GEMM dispatch. FP8 KV is an accuracy-affecting dtype that packs usually fix. Removing --disable-shared-experts-fusion is a removal of a deliberately set safety flag, which an agent treats as a known-good constraint unless it knows the bug it worked around was fixed upstream in that release.

mechanism: SGLANG_USE_AITER switches MLA decode, fused MoE, block-scale FP8 GEMM and norms from Triton defaults to AITER's hand-tuned CDNA3 kernels; a 196K-token prefill budget prefills a whole concurrency batch in one forward; 4 continuous decode steps per scheduler pass amortize Python scheduling overhead across steps.

Llama-3.3-70B FP8 MI300X vLLM: replace (VLLM_USE_TRITON_FLASH_ATTN=0, --dtype bfloat16 --quantization fp8) with AMD's ROCm 7.0-rc1 recipe: VLLM_USE_V1=1, VLLM_V1_USE_PREFILL_DECODE_ATTENTION=1, AMDGCN_USE_BUFFER_OPS=1, VLLM_USE_AITER_TRITON_ROPE=1, TRITON_HIP_ASYNC_COPY_BYPASS_PERMUTE=1, TRITON_HIP_USE_ASYNC_COPY=1, TRITON_HIP_USE_BLOCK_PINGPONG=1, TRITON_HIP_ASYNC_FAST_SWIZZLE=1, VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1, VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_RMSNORM=1; --kv-cache-dtype fp8, --gpu-memory-utilization 0.94, --swap-space 64, --max-num-batched-tokens 131072, --async-scheduling; pre-quantized FP8 checkpoint (dtype auto).
mechanism: V1 engine with the split prefill/decode Triton attention path; AMD Triton backend compiler knobs make every Triton kernel (attention, RoPE) use buffer loads, async global->LDS copies with a fast swizzle, and two-wavefront ping-pong scheduling that overlaps memory and MFMA on CDNA3; AITER RMSNorm and Triton RoPE replace default ops; FP8 KV halves attention bytes; async scheduling overlaps CPU scheduling with GPU execution; 131K batched tokens lets prefill of a full batch run in one step.
why: The four TRITON_HIP_* and AMDGCN_USE_BUFFER_OPS knobs are not vLLM options at all: they are read by the AMD Triton compiler backend and change code generation for every Triton kernel, so neither vLLM --help nor a kernel-level profile names them; finding them means reading the Triton AMD backend source and knowing what async copy and block ping-pong do on CDNA3 LDS/MFMA. Each knob alone is likely a sub-1% change (below the gate) whose value shows only in combination, and the set came from AMD's internal benchmark-docker recipe. The FP8 KV dtype and checkpoint switch are typically pack-fixed accuracy choices.

mechanism: Fused QKV split+RoPE and residual-add+RMSNorm+pad (pads hidden size for the MXFP4 GEMM) cut kernel count per layer; AITER Triton GEMMs for the dense projections; preshuffled MXFP4 scales let the Triton MoE GEMM load scales contiguously; HSA_NO_SCRATCH_RECLAIM keeps kernel scratch memory resident so kernels needing scratch do not stall on reallocation; block size 64 matches the AITER unified-attention tile.
why: The VLLM_* switches are declared in vllm/envs.py and an agent grepping for AITER options would find them, but TRITON_HIP_PRESHUFFLE_SCALES is read by the Triton AMD backend and HSA_NO_SCRATCH_RECLAIM by the ROCm runtime: neither is visible from vLLM, and a kernel profile shows their cost only as unexplained stalls or slower MoE GEMMs. Knowing that block size 64 must match the attention kernel is a co-design fact in the AITER kernel, not a documented vLLM rule.

mechanism: At low concurrency, TP-sharded experts spread every expert's weight read across all 8 GPUs (no all-to-all, no load imbalance) and TP attention beats attention-DP whose ranks would each hold 1-2 requests; at high concurrency EP cuts per-GPU expert weight traffic. trtllm-gen MoE kernels are Blackwell's low-latency path; CUTLASS wins for large prefill-heavy token counts.
why: Each single point needs only discrete flags (ep_size, moe_config.backend, enable_attention_dp), but the right answer is a 3-way interaction that flips with ISL/OSL and concurrency, so an agent at one point must search a 2x2x2 grid where single flips can each look worse (e.g. dropping attention DP without changing EP). It also has to know that TRT-LLM has a TRTLLM (trtllm-gen) MoE backend distinct from CUTLASS and when each wins. The thresholds (16, 32, 64) are only visible from a concurrency sweep the loop never runs, and a pack that fixes the parallelism forbids the EP part outright.

Once the knob is known it is a 2-3 iteration flag search.

DeepSeek-R1 TRT-LLM (tunes 123). FP4 B200: a per-TP x ISL/OSL x CONC table over three regimes: pure-TP MoE with TRTLLM backend at low CONC; TEP (EP=TP, TP attention) above CONC 8-32; DEP (enable_attention_dp true, EP=TP, CUTLASS MoE) at CONC>=256 or 8k/1k CONC>32. With attention DP it adds attention_dp_config {enable_balance: true, timeout_iters: 60, batching_wait_iters: 0}. max_num_tokens = roundup64(CONC+ISL+64) instead of MAX_MODEL_LEN; free_gpu_memory_fraction 0.9->0.8; TP4 added; CONC up to 512. New FP8 B200 recipe: EP=TP, MoE backend DEEPGEMM, attention DP above CONC 32/64. New FP8 H200 recipe: EP=TP, CUTLASS MoE, attention DP above CONC 32/64, cuda graph max 128, free mem 0.75.
mechanism: Attention DP gives each rank its own requests and KV (MLA's single latent head cannot be split across TP ranks, so TP attention replicates KV and repeats the work), which pays once each rank has enough requests; ADP balancing holds ranks so they run context or generation phases together instead of one rank's prefill stalling the other ranks at the MoE all-to-all. max_num_tokens sized to one prompt plus one token per running request bounds the step so a prefill does not balloon decode latency and keeps the activation workspace small, leaving memory for KV. DeepGEMM is the fast FP8 blockwise grouped GEMM on Blackwell.
why: The winning DEP point is a bundle: attention DP alone, without ADP balancing and the right MoE backend, can be slower than TEP because imbalanced ranks wait at every MoE all-to-all, so a one-change-per-iteration loop with a 1% gate rejects the first step of the bundle. enable_balance, timeout_iters and batching_wait_iters are TRT-LLM-internal scheduler knobs whose meaning is only in TRT-LLM source and NVIDIA's deployment guides. The max_num_tokens formula and the crossovers (CONC 8, 16, 32, 256) come from understanding the scheduler and from sweeping concurrency, and the parallelism switch is often fixed by the pack.

mechanism: AITER's CK MHA wins on long prefills (8K) but not on short-prompt, decode-dominated runs, so it is switched by workload; QuickReduce quantizes TP all-reduce payloads to INT4, cutting all-reduce bytes 4x on MI300; more RCCL channels use more CUs for communication; full CUDA graphs for decode plus piecewise for prefill.
why: The knobs are ROCm/AITER-specific env vars (QuickReduce, AITER MHA, MoE scale preshuffle) that appear in AMD engineers' recipes rather than in vLLM's generic docs, so the agent finds them only if its knowledge base lists them. QuickReduce INT4 trades all-reduce precision for bandwidth, which an accuracy-blind 1% throughput gate should not be the one to accept. The AITER-MHA choice reverses with ISL/OSL, so an agent at one point gets a correct local answer but no rule; and the shipped conditional was silently dead (wrong-case variable not passed into the container), which only a per-arm check of the server environment would catch.

mechanism: Disaggregation removes prefill interference from decode and sizes prefill and decode pools separately; wide EP (DEP16/32 over NVLink72) spreads 256 experts so each GPU holds few experts and decode batches per expert grow; MTP speculative decoding raises tokens per decode step at low concurrency.
why: Every ingredient is outside the loop: multiple nodes, a different serving stack (Dynamo orchestrating TRT-LLM workers), KV transfer between workers, and the prefill:decode worker ratio, which can only be set by measuring both pools under the target concurrency. The configuration is a per-concurrency Pareto frontier (one setting per CONC band), not a single best point. MTP also needs draft weights and acceptance on the real data, which the loop's synthetic workload may not reflect.

mechanism: compile_sizes makes torch.compile build a shape-specialized graph for each listed batch size (static shapes let Inductor and the Triton/AITER kernels pick per-shape configs), and dense capture sizes cut the padding from a running batch up to the next captured CUDA graph.
why: compile_sizes is a little-used CompilationConfig field; nothing in a profile points at it, because the gain is the difference between dynamic-shape and static-shape generated kernels and the padding waste between graph sizes, both invisible unless the agent compares kernel variants across batch sizes. It also multiplies start-up compile time by about 70 shapes, which can exceed a harness's server-ready timeout and makes each iteration slower. Choosing the size lists needs the batch-size distribution at the operating point.

mechanism: With the custom ops disabled, these layers are traced as plain PyTorch and torch.compile/Inductor fuses them with their neighbours (residual add + RMSNorm + FP8 quant into one kernel, SiLU-mul + FP8 quant into one kernel), removing kernel launches and the HBM round trips between the separate custom kernels.
why: It is a removal of what the code labels as optimized kernels, and the benefit appears only after the compiler re-fuses the region, so an agent reasoning kernel-by-kernel from a profile would rather speed up or hand-fuse the custom kernels than delete them. Knowing that a '-op' entry in custom_ops hands the op to Inductor's fusion passes, and that on ROCm these were on by default, is vLLM compilation-internals knowledge. Once known it is a single flag and the 6-7% gain clears a 1% gate easily.

New MTP speculative-decoding entries for DSR1 TRT-LLM single node (FP4 B200, FP8 B200, FP8 H200; image 1.1.0rc2.post2): speculative_config decoding_type MTP with num_nextn_predict_layers=3 under TP attention (TRTLLM MoE) and =1 under DP attention (CUTLASS MoE); EP=TP from conc 16-32, DP-attn from conc 64-128; max_num_tokens = ((MTP+1)*max_batch + ISL + 64) rounded to 64; max_batch = CONC/TP under DP-attn; cuda_graph enable_padding, max_batch 512; attention_dp_config batching_wait_iters 0, timeout_iters 60; benchmark client adds --use-chat-template.
mechanism: MTP drafts 1-3 extra tokens per step with DeepSeek's own MTP head, so each decode step (memory-bound at low batch) emits more than one token; at high batch the step becomes compute-bound and verification costs more, so depth drops to 1. The token budget must cover (MTP+1) tokens per request or batches are cut.
why: MTP is a documented feature, but whether it pays depends on acceptance rate, i.e. on the token distribution of the workload (here random prompts, made more realistic with a chat template), which the agent cannot change or see in a kernel profile. The right depth flips with concurrency (3 at low, 1 at high), so one operating point picks one depth and misses the table. It also needs coupled edits (max_num_tokens formula, CUDA-graph padding, MoE backend per regime) and is benchmarked as a separate spec-decoding category, which a pack fixed to non-speculative serving would forbid.
evidence: MTP=3 (TP attn) / MTP=1 (DP attn); speculative_config: decoding_type: MTP num_nextn_predict_layers: ${MTP}; MAX_NUM_TOKENS=$(( ((MTP+1)*MAX_BATCH_SIZE+ISL+64+63)/64*64 )); --use-chat-template

what: DSR1 FP8 B200 TRT-LLM agg: image 1.1.0rc2.post2 -> 1.2.0rc6.post2; MoE backend DEEPGEMM -> TRTLLM (DEEPGEMM kept only for 1k8k conc>=256 with DP-attn, cuda-graph batch CONC/8, KV 0.7); drop EP=TP (ep 1 for most entries), add TP4 entries (conc 8-32), DP-attn only at 1k8k conc 256; piecewise CUDA graphs via torch_compile_config (capture_num_tokens 1..128 then every 256 up to max_num_tokens) at conc>=64 (1k1k, 8k1k) or >=128 (1k8k); delay batching batch_wait_timeout_iters 40, batch_wait_max_tokens_ratio 0.8 for 1k1k conc>=64; cuda_graph max_batch = CONC; KV free fraction 0.7-0.8 (0.75 for TP4 8k1k); TLLM_OVERRIDE_LAYER_NUM=61 to avoid OOM.
mechanism: Piecewise CUDA graphs capture the non-attention parts of mixed prefill/decode iterations, removing launch overhead from prefill-bearing steps that full decode graphs cannot cover; delay batching waits up to 40 iterations to accumulate prefill tokens so context phases run in larger, more efficient chunks; TRTLLM MoE kernels in 1.2 beat DeepGEMM at small/mid batch, and TP-MoE beats EP at these concurrencies; sizing graph batch to CONC avoids wasted capture memory; TLLM_OVERRIDE_LAYER_NUM=61 skips loading the extra MTP layer to save memory.
why: The win is a decision table over ISL/OSL x concurrency x TP (which knobs turn on where), so each campaign point would find only its own row, and the delay-batching knob is counterintuitive (adding wait improves throughput but hurts TTFT). Piecewise graphs with an explicit capture-token list and TLLM_OVERRIDE_LAYER_NUM are TRT-LLM internals of a newer release than the pinned image, and several changes (MoE backend, EP removal, KV fraction, graph batch) interact.

what: New dsr1-fp8-b300-dynamo-trt disagg config (tensorrtllm-runtime:0.8.1.post1): one srt-slurm recipe per concurrency point, 1k1k and 8k1k, MTP and STP. Low conc uses many TP8 decode workers with small batch and MTP3 (ctx1_gen8_tp8_batch1_mtp3 at conc 10); high conc uses few attention-DP decode workers (dp8/dep8) with big batch and MTP1 (ctx3_gen2_dp8_batch512_mtp1 at conc 11264; ctx7_gen1_dep8_batch384 STP at 8k1k conc 3072). Prefill TP4 with dp-attn. Launcher maps dsr1-fp8 to its own model path.
mechanism: Each concurrency gets the prefill:decode worker ratio, decode parallelism (TP for latency, DP-attention/wide EP for throughput), max batch and MTP depth that put it on the Pareto front: deep speculation and TP when batch is tiny and decode is latency-bound; shallow speculation and DP-attention when the batch is large and compute-bound.
why: The content is a Pareto set of multi-node topologies: number of context workers versus generation workers, TP8 versus DEP8 decode, per-worker batch cap and MTP depth, chosen per concurrency. The loop runs one node at one concurrency with fixed parallelism, so it cannot vary worker counts or measure the frontier across concurrencies. Even the single-node parts (MTP depth 3 at low conc, 1 at high conc) only show their value when several operating points are compared.

what: MI355X DSR1 FP4 SGLang disagg (+mtp): image mori-0227-2 -> mori-0227-3; new high-throughput layouts with sub-node prefill workers: 1x DEP4 prefill + 1x DEP8 decode (conc 1024-2048) and 4x DEP4 prefill + 1x DEP8 decode (conc 1024-4096), MTP size 1 or 0. env.sh: for MXFP4 models MoRI FP8 dispatch off, FP4 dispatch and FP8 combine off for all, MXFP4 prefill dispatch cap 12288 tokens, decode dispatch cap 256 -> 160, MoRI IO RDMA queue pairs enlarged (MAX_SEND_WR 16384, MAX_CQE 32768, MAX_SGE 4); MoRI KV transfer backend for MXFP4 too; prefill chunk size tied to dispatch cap x TP; decode no longer passes chunked-prefill-size; PYTHONPATH workaround for AITER.
mechanism: Four small DEP4 prefill workers feed one DEP8 decode worker because 8k-token-class prefill dominates at max throughput, and DEP4 workers waste less on all-to-all than DEP8. Not re-quantizing already-FP4 activations to FP8 for dispatch avoids an extra quantize step and its error; a lower decode dispatch cap shrinks MoRI's per-rank buffers and fits cuda graphs to the real decode batch; deeper RDMA queues keep KV transfers from stalling under many concurrent requests.
why: Most of the gain is in the 4P1D layout with half-node prefill workers, which needs five nodes and a concurrency sweep to place. The MoRI settings (dispatch dtype per checkpoint format, dispatch token caps, RDMA queue-pair depth) are internals of AMD's EP and KV-transfer library that only matter across nodes; the single-node loop never exercises inter-node RDMA, so it neither sees the stalls nor can test the knobs.

what: dsr1-fp8-b200-dynamo-sglang (+mtp) 8k1k: 14 new Pareto recipes resolved from srt-slurm's consolidated 8k1k.yaml. Low latency: one DP-attention TP8 prefill worker (ep 1) feeding 3, 4 or 6 plain TP8 decode workers (ep 8 -> 1, no DP attention) at conc 8-128 (was TEP8 1P1D/1P4D/1P6D). Max throughput: DP-attention prefill with 1-2 workers feeding 1-2 DEP8 decode workers (conc 160-512).
mechanism: For 8k prompts, DP-attention on the prefill worker parallelizes long-prompt attention across ranks without TP communication; for low-latency decode, dense TP MoE (no EP) avoids all-to-all at small batch, and more decode workers per prefill worker keep per-worker batch small. Max-throughput points switch decode to DEP8 for large-batch MoE efficiency.
why: The recipes are a frontier swept over worker counts (1-2 prefill, 1-6 decode), attention parallelism per role and EP on/off per role, for one ISL/OSL; the loop's single node and single concurrency can neither build these layouts nor rank them on tok/s/GPU versus interactivity. The finding that EP should be off on low-latency decode but on for max throughput only appears when both ends of the curve are measured.
evidence: +    # STP low-latency: resolved from 8k1k.yaml zip_override_stp_lowlat; -        ep: 8 -        dp-attn: false +        ep: 1 +        dp-attn: true; decode num-worker: 6 tp: 8 ep: 1

mechanism: With 64 attention heads at TP8 each GPU holds 8 heads, which AITER's MLA decode kernel only supports from vLLM v0.18.0; the upgrade lets the AITER master switch turn on AITER MLA/MoE/GEMM paths. INT4 quick-reduce quantizes the TP all-reduce payload (the commit cites 2.2x vs 1.17x speedup for INT4 vs INT8 quick-reduce). block-size 1 is the page size AITER's MLA decode is built for. TP4 and TP4/EP4 add more replicas per node for throughput-oriented points.
effect: Not stated in numbers; commit cites quick-reduce benchmark speedups (INT4 2.2x vs INT8 1.17x).
why: The enabling step is outside the loop: AITER MLA was unusable for 8 heads per GPU in the v0.16.0 image, and the fix arrives only with the v0.18.0 image, which the agent cannot change. Within the image, INT4 quick-reduce is a documented env var an agent could try, but it is a lossy all-reduce whose acceptability needs an accuracy check, and the RMSNorm TP<8 carve-out exists only because someone saw an accuracy failure, which a throughput gate never shows. TP4 and TP4/EP4 are new parallelism layouts that a pack fixing TP rules out, and their value appears only across the concurrency sweep.

mechanism: Kimi K2.5 has 64 heads, so TP8 leaves 8 heads per GPU, which AITER's MLA decode did not support before the patch tracked in vllm issue 35641 (shipped in v0.18.0); the new image also carries tuned Triton fused-MoE configs (vllm PR 35093). With the patch, the AITER master switch can route MLA decode, MoE and GEMMs to AITER kernels. max-num-seqs 256 lets the scheduler batch up to the sweep's top concurrency.
why: The blocking constraint (AITER MLA rejects 8 heads per rank) is fixed upstream in a newer image the loop cannot install; inside the old image VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 simply fails or falls back, so the gate sees nothing to keep. Backporting would mean writing head padding or a kernel variant for AITER MLA, an architectural change the agent rarely attempts, and knowing that the fix exists requires tracking the vLLM issue tracker. The Triton MoE tuning half is reachable in-loop (tile tables for the measured shapes), but only for the point being measured.

mechanism: Removing the two disables lets v0.19 pick FlashInfer's FP8 MoE and DeepGEMM kernels, faster than the fallback Triton MoE on Blackwell. The FlashInfer MNNVL all-reduce is a low-latency NVLink one/two-shot all-reduce for small decode payloads. FP8 KV halves cache bytes, raising batch capacity and cutting decode attention bandwidth. A 2048-token CUDA-graph ceiling keeps large decode batches graphed. Capping batched tokens at 2*ISL bounds prefill chunks so decode steps are not stalled; stream-interval 20 cuts per-token streaming overhead.
why: Most pieces are documented flags an agent could try one at a time, but the bundle needs knowledge the loop does not supply: that the MoE disables were workarounds for bugs in an older image and are now safe to remove, and that FlashInfer exposes an MNNVL all-reduce backend selectable by env var. The EP bug (-ge 1) is a launcher error only visible by reading the script against the sweep matrix. FP8 KV and the added EP layouts are often fixed by the pack, and their value lies at high concurrency across the sweep, not at one point.

what: New config kimik2.5-fp4-gb200-dynamo-vllm (new framework dynamo-vllm: Dynamo frontend + vLLM v0.18.0-cu130 workers, NixlConnector KV transfer, FLASHINFER_MLA): disaggregated multi-node recipes from NVIDIA/srt-slurm sa-submission-q2-2026. 1k1k: 1P1D DEP4 prefill / DEP16 decode (throughput) and 1P4D DEP4 / TEP4 (latency). 8k1k: 1P4D DEP4/TEP4, 3P1D DEP4/DEP16, 5P1D DEP4/DEP8, 6P1D DEP4/DEP16; conc up to 4096. Runner clones NVIDIA/srt-slurm and maps the vLLM image.
mechanism: Disaggregation runs prefill and decode on separate GPU pools so long prefills never stall decode steps, and each pool gets its own parallelism: prefill on DP-attention + EP4, decode on wide EP16 with DP attention (spreading Kimi's 384 experts over 16 GPUs, so per-GPU expert weight drops and batch grows) at the throughput end, or TP-attention EP4 decode replicas at the latency end. The P:D ratio (1:4 to 6:1) matches prefill capacity to decode demand for each ISL/OSL; KV moves over NVLink/RDMA via NIXL.
why: Every ingredient lies outside a one-node loop: the recipe spans several GB200 trays (NVL72), uses a different framework (Dynamo) and a KV-transfer path, and its main levers (P:D worker ratio, DEP16 vs TEP4 decode, prefill vs decode parallelism) are topology choices whose value appears only across a concurrency sweep up to 4096. The right ratio depends on ISL/OSL (1P4D for latency vs 6P1D for 8k1k throughput), which needs workload-level capacity reasoning, not a 1% gate on one point.

New config kimik2.5-fp4-gb200-dynamo-trt (new framework dynamo-trt: Dynamo frontend + TensorRT-LLM, image ai-dynamo/tensorrtllm-runtime 1.1.0-dev.2): 14 disaggregated STP (no MTP) recipes from NVIDIA/srt-slurm sa-submission-q2-2026. 1k1k: ctx1 DEP4 with gen 4xTEP8 (batch 128), 5xTEP4 (batch 8), 1xDEP16 (batch 32), 1xDEP32 (batch 64), 1xDEP8 (batch 768), ctx2 DEP4 with gen DEP16 (batch 256) or DEP32 (batch 128), each pinned to its own concurrency list (4 up to 6452). 8k1k: gen TEP8 batch 1, TEP4 batch 16/32, and ctx2/3/5/7 DEP4 prefill against DEP16 or DEP8 decode for conc 333-2253. EPLB off in all. Same model on dynamo-vllm in id 451.
mechanism: Separates prefill and decode pools; decode width and attention mode are chosen per concurrency band: tensor-parallel attention (TEP4/TEP8) with small max batch for the latency end, data-parallel attention with wide expert parallelism (DEP8 to DEP32 across NVL72 trays) for the throughput end, where spreading 384 experts over up to 32 GPUs shrinks per-GPU MoE weight reads and lets each rank batch hundreds of sequences. The number of prefill workers (1 to 7) is scaled to the 8k-token prompt load so decode is never starved. Each recipe's max batch is matched to its concurrency points.
why: These are fourteen multi-node points on an NVL72 rack, each a distinct topology (prefill count, decode width up to 32 GPUs, TEP vs DEP, max batch) tied to specific concurrencies; nothing in a one-node, one-point loop can express them. Choosing them needs a model of prefill vs decode throughput per ISL/OSL and a Pareto sweep across concurrency, and the gains come from cross-tray NVLink expert parallelism that does not exist on a single 8-GPU node. The TRT-LLM + Dynamo stack is also a different framework and image.

what: New config dsv4-fp4-b200-sglang (DeepSeek-V4-Pro, lmsysorg/sglang:deepseek-v4-blackwell, TP8) with three SGLang-cookbook recipes chosen inside the script by concurrency: low-latency (conc <= 32) TP-only with --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4, chunked prefill 4096, --disable-flashinfer-autotune; balanced (<= 128) and max-throughput (> 128) with DP attention (--dp-size 8), --moe-a2a-backend deepep (forces EP8), DeepEP normal dispatch/combine on 96 SMs, SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=256, cuda-graph-max-bs 64, max-running-requests 128 or 256; SGLANG_JIT_DEEPGEMM_PRECOMPILE=0; MTP and prefix caching off for a baseline; new b200-dsv4 runners.
mechanism: At low concurrency, TP attention plus the FlashInfer MXFP4 MoE minimizes per-token latency; at higher concurrency, DP attention removes the attention all-reduce and lets each rank batch its own requests, while DeepEP all-to-all dispatches tokens to whole experts on each GPU, so per-GPU MoE GEMMs are larger; the SM budget and dispatch-token cap size DeepEP's buffers for the batch.
why: A day-0 recipe for a new model in a model-specific image. Its core is a regime switch: one parallel layout (TP-only) below conc 32 and another (DP attention + DeepEP EP8) above, which a campaign fixed to one concurrency and one layout would never set up, and whose crossover only a sweep shows. The DeepEP knobs (SMs given to communication, dispatch tokens per rank) trade compute SMs against all-to-all bandwidth and must match the batch size, which needs knowledge of DeepEP internals rather than a flag search.

Prefill: DP8+EP, enforce-eager, max-num-batched-tokens 32768, CPU expert offload (offload-group-size 3, offload-num-in-group 1, offload-prefetch-step 2) required to fit. Decode: TP8 or DEP16, FULL_DECODE_ONLY cudagraphs, use_fp4_indexer_cache, fuse_allreduce_rms off, stream-interval 50. Env: VLLM_USE_NCCL_SYMM_MEM=1, NCCL_MNNVL_ENABLE=1, NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=1, UCX_CUDA_IPC_ENABLE_MNNVL=y.
mechanism: Disaggregation separates compute-bound prefill (wide DP/EP, eager, big token budget) from latency-bound decode (TP8 at low concurrency, DEP16 at high), and the P:D ratio is scaled per concurrency band so neither side starves; MNNVL/NVLS/symmetric-memory NCCL use the NVL72 fabric for cross-tray collectives and KV transfer.
why: Every lever is a multi-node topology choice: how many prefill workers per decode worker (1p1d vs 3p1d vs 7p1d), decode TP8 vs DEP16 across trays, and CPU expert offload on prefill just to fit. The loop has one 8-GPU node and a fixed TP, so it cannot instantiate a P/D split at all, let alone sweep the ratio across concurrency bands. The low-concurrency recipe was mirrored from NVIDIA's srt-slurm recipes and the others extrapolated from Kimi-K2.5's pattern, i.e. the knowledge came from outside the measured system.
evidence: Low-conc 1p1d-dep8-tep8 (4 nodes, mirrored from NVIDIA srt-slurm PR #71 with offload kept and numa-bind dropped); mid 1p1d-dep8-dep16 (6 nodes) and high 3p1d-dep8-dep16 (10 nodes) hand-rolled; 'CPU/DRAM expert offload — required for fit. The loop measures one concurrency with a pack-fixed TP size and 8 GPUs, so it can neither move to 4 GPUs nor switch TP to DP. The individual flags (fp4 indexer cache, capture size) are documented and reachable, but the schedule itself came from a vendor's offline sweep.

dsv4-fp4-gb300-dynamo-sglang overhaul by an SGLang maintainer (staging image deepseek-v4-grace-blackwell-dev): decode becomes WideEP DEP16 for most points with P:D 1:1 (conc 1024, 5 nodes), 4:1 (1024), 8:1 (4096, 12 nodes), 10:1 (8192, 14 nodes), and DEP12 decode with 12 prefill workers at conc 21504 (15 nodes); TP4/TP4 1P1D at conc 1. Max point adds a KV-aware Dynamo router (router-mode kv, overlap weight 0, queue threshold 64, temperature 0.5), DeepEP NVL chunk tuning (num_sms 88, send/recv chunk tokens), SGLANG_CLIP_MAX_NEW_TOKENS_ESTIMATION=8, SGLANG_OPT_USE_ONLINE_COMPRESS=1, SGLANG_OPT_FP8_WO_A_GEMM=1, decode load-balance total_requests, polling interval 8, swa ratio 0.056, cuda-graph-max-bs 1280, MegaMoE token caps 8192 prefill / 1280 decode; lm-eval re-enabled.
mechanism: Per-point balance of prefill capacity against one wide decode engine; DEP12 sized so 21504 requests fit KV and graphs (1792 per rank); clipping the new-token estimate lets the decode scheduler admit more requests at once; the router spreads prefill load; tuned DeepEP chunking and FP8 wo_a GEMM cut communication and GEMM time.
why: This is a co-design of deployment shape and scheduler internals across 15 nodes: P:D ratios up to 12:1, an unusual 12-GPU decode width, router policy, and admission-control env vars such as SGLANG_CLIP_MAX_NEW_TOKENS_ESTIMATION that only matter when tens of thousands of requests are in flight. None of it can be instantiated on one node, and the env switches are undocumented internals known to the SGLang developers who wrote them.
evidence: switch decode to WideEP TP=16 across most concurrency points (TP=12 at the 21504 max-concurrency point) ... router-mode: "kv" ... SGLANG_CLIP_MAX_NEW_TOKENS_ESTIMATION: "8"

what: dsr1-fp4-mi355x-sglang-disagg (+mtp), MI355X multi-node with MoRI: image rocm/sgl-dev sglang-0.5.9 mori-0227-3 -> lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.10.post1-rocm720-mi35x-20260501; checkpoint amd/DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4 -> MXFP4-v2; MoRI FP4 dispatch (SGLANG_MORI_DISPATCH_DTYPE=auto) + FP8 combine (SGLANG_MORI_FP8_COMB=true); prefill SDMA (MORI_ENABLE_SDMA) + --enable-two-batch-overlap; SGLANG_ENABLE_SPEC_V2=1, SGLANG_ENABLE_OVERLAP_PLAN_STREAM=1, decode MTP 1 -> 2; prefill topology 4xDEP4 -> 2xDEP8; MoRI tuning (QP per transfer 4, 4 workers, IO QP/CQE limits, TC/SL from NIC QoS), dispatch token caps prefill 8192 / decode 512, MoE input-token caps 32768 / 2703 (scaled by MTP+1), pre-allocate 32 requests; prefill dp: max-running 4096, context 9217, max-total-tokens 131072; decode dp: cuda-graph bs 1-512, tokenizer workers 32, stream-interval 100; conc 4096 added.
mechanism: Lower-precision EP all-to-all (FP4 dispatch, FP8 combine) halves or quarters MoE communication bytes; SDMA engines move data without SMs, letting two-batch overlap hide prefill all-to-all behind compute; spec-v2 and overlapped plan stream hide CPU scheduling of MTP; fewer, wider prefill workers reduce cross-node EP traffic; NIC QP/QoS tuning raises RDMA KV-transfer throughput.
why: The change spans a new image, a new quantized checkpoint, multi-node prefill/decode topology, NIC-level RDMA QoS/QP parameters, and MoRI internals (SDMA, dispatch dtypes, token caps). It also trades accuracy: per 609, FP8 combine fails GSM8K at high concurrency, a regression a throughput-gated loop would book as a win unless it evaluates accuracy every iteration. Benchmark mode also runs with --ep-dispatch-algorithm fake, stripped only in eval mode, so the measured EP traffic is synthetic.
evidence: Enable fp4 disp / fp8 combine feature on mori; Enable Mori SDMA + two batch overlapping feature ... export SGLANG_MORI_FP8_COMB=true ... PREFILL_SDMA_ENV="MORI_ENABLE_SDMA=true"

mechanism: GLM-5 FP8 fits in 4 x 288 GB MI355X, so TP4 halves the GPUs per replica and the all-reduce fan-out; on the per-GPU throughput axis that roughly doubles throughput/GPU at a given interactivity and lets each replica carry higher concurrency (hence conc up to 256). Setting --cuda-graph-max-bs to CONC makes decode batches up to the benchmark concurrency replay a captured graph instead of falling back to eager; --max-running-requests caps the scheduler at the same size.
effect: Not quantified; PR says 'Turn to tp=4 for best perf'.
why: The main lever is the tensor-parallel size, which Arbor packs normally fix, and its payoff is in throughput per GPU, a normalization the agent's absolute tok/s gate at one concurrency does not see (TP4 on its own looks slower per replica). Seeing it requires knowing the weights' footprint against 288 GB HBM and comparing operating points across the Pareto curve rather than one point. The cuda-graph-max-bs part alone is easy: a profile at conc 256 would show eager decode.

dsv4-fp4-b300-vllm-mtp: image v0.20.0-cu130 -> v0.20.2; TP8 MTP range narrowed from conc 1-64 to 1-8, and new DEP points { tp: 4, ep: 4, dp-attn: true } at conc 256-1024 (1k1k) and 256-512 (8k1k); with DP attention the script passes --moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe and --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 (instead of 2*ISL), and runs --tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel.
mechanism: At high concurrency, DP attention gives each of 4 ranks its own batch and KV (no attention all-reduce, no KV replicated across TP ranks), and EP shards the experts, so a 4-GPU replica carries far more concurrent sequences per GPU. The deep_gemm_mega_moe backend is DeepGEMM's MoE path for the expert-parallel layout (the same MegaMoE choice the GB200 DEP8 disagg recipe uses, id 703); per its name it handles the EP token dispatch, grouped FP4 GEMMs and combine as one fused path, cutting the all-to-all and launch overhead that dominates EP MoE at these batch sizes (the PR does not explain it). A 2048-token prefill chunk keeps per-step latency bounded on each DP rank. TP8 is kept only for the low-concurrency latency end.
why: The win is a different parallel layout (DP-attention + EP on half the GPUs) chosen per concurrency band, which an Arbor pack fixes and which only pays at concurrencies far above a single measured point; at conc 1-8 it would lose. It also needs the agent to know that vLLM v0.20.x exposes a DeepGEMM 'mega MoE' backend and that it is meant for the EP/DP layout, and to co-tune the batched-token budget with it. Three coupled changes (layout, MoE backend, chunk size) each look neutral or worse alone.

what: New glm5-fp8-b200-dynamo-sglang disaggregated multi-node config (sglang v0.5.11-cu130, Dynamo 1.1.0, NIXL KV transfer) with 16 srt-slurm recipes for 1k1k and 8k1k: max-throughput points are 1 prefill node (TP8 + DP8 attention, dp-lm-head, total_tokens load balancing, chunked-prefill 65536, max-prefill-tokens 8192) + 1 decode node (DP8 attention, max-running-requests/cuda-graph-max-bs 2560) at conc 2576; low-latency points are 1 DEP8 prefill node + up to 8 decode nodes each a plain TP8 worker (max-running/cuda-graph bs 64) at conc 32-512. Both sides use NSA trtllm backends, flashinfer_trtllm MoE, flashinfer allreduce fusion, fp8 KV, no radix cache, stream-interval 30.
mechanism: Splitting prefill and decode onto separate nodes removes prefill interference from decode steps (steady ITL) and lets each phase use its own parallelism: DP attention on the prefill side and on high-throughput decode (each rank holds its own requests' KV, no attention all-reduce, thousands of concurrent sequences), and plain TP8 decode workers replicated 8x for low latency (smallest per-token step). The P:D ratio and decode layout are chosen per Pareto region.
why: Every point uses two to nine 8-GPU nodes and a KV-transfer fabric (NIXL/Dynamo), which an agent confined to one node cannot run or measure. The decisions are joint across prefill/decode node counts, per-phase parallelism and per-phase batch caps, and each is right only for one region of the throughput-latency curve, so a single-operating-point loop with a 1% gate has no gradient toward them. The low-latency shape (1 DEP prefill feeding 8 TP decode replicas) is a fleet-sizing decision, not a server flag.
evidence: prefill_nodes: 1, decode_nodes: 8, decode_workers: 8 (lowlat); decode: enable-dp-attention: true, max-running-requests: 2560, cuda-graph-max-bs: 2560 (maxtpt, conc 2576); disaggregation-transfer-backend: nixl

dsv4-fp4-gb300-dynamo-sglang disagg (1p1d..12p1d, DEP4 prefill / DEP12-16 decode): wherever SGLANG_OPT_USE_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE is on, add SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_USE_FP4_ACTS=1 and SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_USE_MXF4_KIND=1 (W4A4 MXFP4 MegaMoE); drop SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=0; image staging deepseek-v4-grace-blackwell-dev -> nightly-dev-cu13-20260514; custom_tokenizer for the nightly. Re-landed later as 802.
mechanism: MegaMoE is DeepGEMM's fused EP dispatch + expert GEMM + combine kernel. With FP4 activations and the MXF4 MMA kind, activations are quantized to MXFP4 so the expert GEMMs run W4A4 on Blackwell FP4 tensor cores (about 2x FP8 FLOPs) and the dispatched token payload shrinks, cutting both MoE compute and NVLink all-to-all bytes.
why: The switch is two undocumented SGLANG_OPT_* env vars that exist only in the MegaMoE path of a nightly image, so the agent would have to find them in source. More importantly it lowers activation precision to FP4, a quantization change that packs usually fix and that the 1% throughput gate cannot judge (it needs an accuracy check). Its payoff is largest in the wide-EP DEP16 decode across GB300 nodes, where dispatch bytes matter, which a one-node loop never runs.

what: minimaxm2.5-fp8-h100-vllm: image v0.21.0 -> v0.19.1-cu130 (a downgrade); search space TP4/EP4 conc 4-64 -> TP8/EP8 conc 4-128; compilation-config PIECEWISE -> '{"mode":3,"pass_config":{"fuse_minimax_qk_norm":true}}' (full+piecewise graphs plus the MiniMax QK-norm fusion pass); drops max-num-seqs 256, explicit max-model-len and --no-enable-prefix-caching; adds tool-call/reasoning parsers.
mechanism: TEP8 spreads the FP8 MoE and attention over all 8 H100s, so weights per GPU halve and KV capacity grows, letting the batch reach C=128 before saturating; full CUDA graphs and the fused QK RMSNorm cut decode launch overhead.
effect: TEP=8 peaks at C=128 with 26,923 total tok/s, +178% vs the TEP=4 peak at C=32 (local sweep)
why: The gain is a topology change (TP4/EP4 -> TP8/EP8) whose value shows at a concurrency (C=128) beyond the old recipe's sweep end; a loop fixed at one TP and one concurrency would not see it, and packs usually fix TP. It also rolled the image back to v0.19.1, which the loop cannot do. The QK-norm fusion pass is a documented vLLM pass_config option and would be easy alone.

what: New glm5-fp4-gb300-dynamo-sglang disagg recipes (nvidia/GLM-5-NVFP4, sglang v0.5.11-cu130, dynamo 1.1.0), ported from upstream srt-slurm PR #152: 8k1k max-throughput 5p1d/7p1d/10p1d with TP4 DP-attention prefill workers and one wide-EP TP32/EP32 DP-attention decode worker across 8 nodes (13-18 nodes total); low-latency variants with TP4 decode workers per node; nixl KV transfer, MNNVL, SGLANG_MOE_NVFP4_DISPATCH=1, DeepEP max dispatch tokens 512, trtllm NSA backends, flashinfer_trtllm MoE for prefill and flashinfer_cutedsl for decode, flashinfer allreduce fusion, fp8 KV.
mechanism: Disaggregation lets compute-bound prefill and memory-bound decode scale separately; one 32-GPU wide-EP decode worker spreads GLM-5's experts so each GPU holds few experts and decode batches are large, and NVFP4 dispatch halves all-to-all bytes over MNNVL.
why: The design is a multi-node topology: a prefill:decode worker ratio, a 32-GPU EP decode group over NVLink-switch, KV transfer via nixl and a multi-frontend Dynamo router. A one-node loop cannot run any of it, and the per-topology choices (5/7/10 prefill workers per decode, TP32 vs TP4 decode) only make sense across the throughput-latency curve, not at one point. It was ported from NVIDIA's srt-slurm recipe, i.e. it came from outside knowledge.
evidence: # 5p1d wide-EP. 13 nodes (5P @ TP=4 + 1D @ TP=32 on 8 nodes). ... SGLANG_MOE_NVFP4_DISPATCH: "1"

minimaxm2.5-fp8-h200-vllm (v0.20.1): TP8 conc 4-128 -> TP4 conc 1-256; --kv-cache-dtype fp8, --attention-backend FLASHINFER --enable-flashinfer-autotune, --moe-backend triton, compilation-config mode 3 PIECEWISE + fuse_minimax_qk_norm, max-num-seqs 512, max-num-batched-tokens 32768; env VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0, VLLM_BLOCKSCALE_FP8_GEMM_FLASHINFER=0, VLLM_FLOAT32_MATMUL_PRECISION=high, SAFETENSORS_FAST_GPU=1. Same model family as 757 (H100).
mechanism: TP4 halves the GPUs per replica, which raises tok/s per GPU for a ~230B MoE that fits in 4 H200s; fp8 KV doubles KV capacity so a TP4 instance can batch to 256; FlashInfer attention with autotune and the Triton MoE are the faster kernels on Hopper for this model; turning off DeepGEMM and FlashInfer block-scale FP8 GEMM routes the block-FP8 linears to the path that is faster at these shapes; fused QK-norm cuts launches.
why: Each knob is a documented vLLM flag or env var, but the win is a joint setting of about ten of them plus a TP change (8 -> 4) that packs usually fix and whose benefit is per-GPU throughput at high concurrency. Two of the changes are removals of supposedly faster libraries (DeepGEMM, FlashInfer block-scale GEMM) that only pay at these specific Hopper shapes, which an agent would not try first; a one-knob-per-iteration loop at a 1% gate would need many accepted steps in the right order.

what: dsr1-fp4-mi355x-sglang-disagg (+mtp): replace SGLANG_MORI_FP8_COMB=true (which failed GSM8K far below the 0.95 golden score at high concurrency) with per-phase combine dtypes MORI_COMBINE_DTYPE_PREFILL=fp8_direct_cast and MORI_COMBINE_DTYPE_DECODE=fp8 (blockwise-scaled FP8 combine); SGLANG_ENABLE_OVERLAP_PLAN_STREAM 1 -> 0; image -> sglang-rocm v0.5.12-20260519; MTP topology 1P2D TP4 -> 1xDEP8 prefill + 1xDEP8 decode (MTP size 1) and a new non-MTP DEP8+DEP8 point at conc 128-512; when DP and EP are both on, max-running-requests = max bench conc, MoRI decode dispatch tokens per rank = conc / dp_ranks, MoE max input = 0.7 x that x ranks, inter-kernel switch threshold = 2 x dispatch tokens.
mechanism: Keeps the bandwidth saving of FP8 MoE combine (half the all-to-all bytes of BF16) while restoring accuracy with a blockwise-scaled FP8 combine in decode; sizing MoRI dispatch buffers to the actual per-rank load avoids over-provisioned buffers and picks the right intra/inter-node dispatch kernel.
why: The earlier FP8 combine was a throughput win that a 1% throughput gate would have kept: it only failed on GSM8K at high concurrency, so the defect is invisible to the loop's measurement. The fix depends on a MoRI combine with quantization correction that arrived in a new image, a per-phase dtype choice (prefill vs decode), and DEP8 prefill and decode on separate nodes, none of which a single-node one-point loop can explore.

what: dsv4-fp4-mi355x-sglang: image -> rocm/sgl-dev ...f96ac98-20260526-DSv4; adds --mem-fraction-static 0.90 and --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.15 'to avoid kvcache pool full issue on high conc'; AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND 1 -> 0 (undoes the flag added in 741); dp-attn sweep end 1024/512 -> 2048. Series 741 -> 755 -> 771.
mechanism: DSV4 has separate KV pools for sliding-window and full/compressed attention layers; lowering swa-full-tokens-ratio to 0.15 shifts memory from the SWA pool to the full pool, and mem-fraction 0.90 enlarges the total, so the full pool no longer fills at conc 1024-2048 and requests are not stalled or retracted, raising peak throughput.
why: The flag is a documented SGLang argument and the failure (KV pool full) appears in the server log, but only at concurrencies (1024-2048) above the previous sweep end, so a loop fixed at a lower operating point never triggers it. Choosing 0.15 also requires knowing DSV4's hybrid KV layout: how much SWA state each request needs relative to its full-attention tokens.
evidence: +    --mem-fraction-static 0.90 \n+    --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.15  ... 'Add args to avoid kvcache pool full issue on high conc'

what: New glm5-fp8-gb300-dynamo-sglang disagg recipes (zai-org/GLM-5-FP8, sglang v0.5.11-cu130, dynamo 1.1.0), resolved from upstream srt-slurm PR #160: 8k1k high-throughput with up to 14 TP4 DP-attention prefill workers and one wide-EP decode worker at TP/EP 16, 24, 32 or 40 (DeepEP low_latency a2a, 32 redundant experts, static dispatch, moe-dense-tp 1, dp-lm-head, stream-interval 30, skip-tokenizer-init), conc 2800 etc.; low-latency variants with TP4 decode workers per node; 1k1k hightpt/lowlat; nixl transfer, NATS request plane, 10 frontends. Sibling of 758 (FP4).
mechanism: Disaggregated prefill/decode with a wide-EP decode group: expert weights spread over 16-40 GPUs so each holds few experts and decode runs large DP-attention batches; redundant experts with static dispatch balance expert load; low-latency DeepEP kernels keep all-to-all latency down; many prefill workers keep the decode group fed at 8k input.
why: Every axis that matters (prefill worker count, decode EP width 16-40, redundant-expert count, frontend count) is a multi-node topology choice tuned along the whole throughput-latency curve. The loop has one node and one operating point, so it cannot run or compare these, and the recipe came from NVIDIA's srt-slurm repository rather than from iteration.
evidence: decode: tensor-parallel-size: 32 ... ep-num-redundant-experts: 32, ep-dispatch-algorithm: static, moe-a2a-backend: deepep, deepep-mode: low_latency

what: glm5-fp4-gb300-dynamo-sglang 8k1k low-latency (follows 758), mirroring NVIDIA/srt-slurm#175: adds a 1p17d topology (1 TP4 prefill worker, 17 TP4 decode workers, 18 nodes) at conc 12; per-topology decode max-running-requests and cuda-graph-max-bs lowered from a flat 4096 to 128/64/32/16/1 and benchmark concurrency from 1024 to 128/64/32/16/12.
mechanism: At low latency each decode worker should carry only a handful of requests: spreading 12 requests over 17 TP4 decode workers gives each about one, so per-token latency is that of batch-1 decode; sizing cuda-graph-max-bs to the real batch avoids capturing and reserving memory for 4096-wide graphs.
why: The new point is an 18-node topology whose only purpose is the extreme low-latency end of the Pareto curve; a one-node loop at a fixed concurrency neither runs it nor values it. The cuda-graph and max-running-requests sizing alone would be easy, but it is tied to the per-topology concurrency.

minimaxm2.5-fp8-mi325x-vllm: pin --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA (vLLM PR #36702 had flipped the ROCm dense full-attention default from ROCM_AITER_FA to ROCM_ATTN); export VLLM_ROCM_SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=1 only for shapes where AITER has a gfx942 ASM paged-attention kernel (TP2/EP1 conc<=16, TP8/EP8 conc<=64), off elsewhere because pa_fwd_asm crashes ('cannot get heuristic kernel') for MiniMax's gqa=6 block 32; --compilation-config mode 3 PIECEWISE; fuse_minimax_qk_norm deliberately omitted (NameError on ROCm, the pass is imported only under is_cuda()); image pinned to v0.20.2 because v0.21.0 crashes in AITER MoE graph capture. Follows the upstream vllm-project/recipes#481; 792 bumps the image to v0.22.0 the same week.
mechanism: AITER's flash-attention backend is much faster than the generic ROCM_ATTN on MI325X for MiniMax's dense attention; the shuffled KV layout lets decode auto-dispatch to AITER's hand-written ASM paged-attention kernel where one exists for the shape.
effect: Recovers the ~38% MI325X throughput regression from the upstream default flip; v0.20.2 + recipe: 2030 tok/s total on a 100-prompt run (TP=4)
why: Switching the attention backend is a documented flag and a profile would show the slow attention kernel, so that part is easy once someone suspects it. The rest needs knowledge the loop does not have: that an upstream default changed between versions (a regression only visible against older numbers), and which (TP, EP, concurrency) shapes have an ASM kernel in AITER's gfx942 heuristic table, since the shuffle flag crashes outside them. The per-shape toggle also only matters across the sweep; a loop at one point would set it once.
evidence: recover the ~38% MI325X throughput regression introduced when vLLM PR #36702 ... flipped the dense full-attention default on ROCm from ROCM_AITER_FA to ROCM_ATTN

what: dsr1-fp4-mi355x-sglang-disagg-mtp split into -1k1k-mtp and -8k1k-mtp, image -> sglang-rocm v0.5.12.post1-20260529; 8k1k: decode MTP draft size raised to 3 on every point (was 1 or 2), 1P2D TP8 conc 64-256 -> 32-64, DEP8+DEP8 points at 640/512, 256, 128 and 64; re-applies the per-phase MoRI combine dtypes of 766 to the rewritten dual-engine env.sh; AITER_LOG_LEVEL=ERROR.

what: New qwen3.5-fp4-b200-trt (Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-NVFP4, TRT-LLM 1.3.0rc18): sparse point list over TP/TEP/DEP; MAX_BATCH_SIZE per layout (DEP4 256, DEP8 128, TP2/EP2 at conc>=32 32, TP>=4 512); MoE backend CUTEDSL with attention-DP, TRTLLM otherwise; attention_dp batching_wait_iters 10; non-DP batch_wait_timeout_iters 50 and batch_wait_max_tokens_ratio 0.45; enable_chunked_prefill false; fp8 KV at 0.9; use_low_precision_moe_combine; max_num_tokens 16384 (1k1k) / 32768 (8k1k).
mechanism: Batch-wait knobs hold the scheduler until enough tokens accumulate, raising GEMM efficiency per step; CuteDSL MoE is the faster grouped GEMM under DEP's per-rank token counts; per-layout batch caps keep graphs and KV within budget.

The batch-wait knobs are counterintuitive (delaying work to make it more efficient) and pay off only at concurrencies where steps are under-filled.

what: minimaxm3-fp8-b200/b300-vllm (+mtp): add --moe-backend marlin when expert parallelism is off (TP-only rows).

The gate on 'no EP' encodes that the win holds only in the memory-bound, low-batch regime, which one operating point cannot show.

Duplicate changelog entry: id 878.
mechanism: TBO splits each step into two micro-batches so one's MoE/communication overlaps the other's attention; it needs enough tokens per step to split, hence the high-concurrency gate, and GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=5 gives ROCm enough hardware queues for the two streams to actually run concurrently. The index-cache override reuses DSv4's sparse-attention indexer top-k selection across 4 layers instead of recomputing it every layer, cutting indexer work at long context. Explicit graph sizes and more KV memory raise batch capacity.
why: TBO only pays off above a token-count threshold and costs below it; the agent at one operating point would either never try it (low concurrency) or keep it unconditionally, and the threshold differs by ISL (1024 vs 256). GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES is a ROCm runtime variable whose relevance (stream concurrency limited by hardware queues) is not visible from the framework flags; without it TBO may show no gain and be rejected. The index_topk_freq override changes the model's computation (an approximation), so it requires knowing DSv4's indexer can be shared across layers and accepting an accuracy trade a speed-only gate would not judge.

what: dsv4-fp4-mi355x-sglang: image v0.5.13-20260612 -> v0.5.13.post1-rocm720-mi35x-20260618; export SGLANG_DP_USE_GATHERV=1 (all_gatherv + reduce_scatterv for the TP+DP-attention config); chunked-prefill-size 8192 -> ISL (ISL*TP with DP attention). Follows id 859.
mechanism: With DP attention, ranks hold different token counts before the MoE; the default path pads every rank to the max and all-gathers/all-reduces the padded tensor, while gatherv/reduce_scatterv move only each rank's real tokens. Tying the prefill chunk to ISL makes each prompt one chunk per rank, which at 1k ISL means 1024-token chunks that interleave with decode instead of 8192-token stalls.
why: SGLANG_DP_USE_GATHERV is an environment switch in SGLang's DP communication code, not a documented server flag; the agent would have to see padded collectives in the profile and read the code to find it, and the benefit depends on token imbalance across DP ranks at high concurrency. The chunk-size rule (chunk = ISL, times DP) encodes the workload's prompt length and SGLang's division of the chunk across DP ranks; at one ISL the agent could tune the number but not learn the rule.

mechanism: DP attention removes duplicated KV across TP ranks at high concurrency; the prefill delayer holds prefill until DP ranks can prefill together so no rank stalls decode at the MoE sync; local-control broadcast and a DP LM head cut per-step control and logits traffic; higher schedule conservativeness avoids KV over-admission and retraction; recv-interval 1 keeps all ranks' queues fresh. Keeping the radix cache structure but forcing misses keeps the faster radix-cache scheduler path without reusing prefixes.
why: Several knobs are counterintuitive: delaying prefill, admitting requests more conservatively, and keeping the radix cache on while forcing every lookup to miss (the obvious --disable-radix-cache switches SGLang to a different, slower cache path). Their value appears only with DP attention at high concurrency, where rank imbalance dominates, so an agent at a TP or low-concurrency point would reject them. SGLANG_RADIX_FORCE_MISS is an environment variable, not a documented flag.

what: dsv4-fp4-b200-sglang: image lmsysorg/sglang:deepseek-v4-blackwell (pinned digest) -> mainline nightly-dev-cu13-20260628-da802ddc; DEP conc-end 512 -> 1024. The changelog names only the image, but the script is retuned: obsolete SGLANG_OPT_* flags dropped (JIT norm, JIT indexer metadata, topk v2, custom all-reduce v2, DeepGEMM precompile off); DP-attention path switches --moe-a2a-backend deepep -> megamoe with SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_USE_FP4_ACTS=1, _USE_MXF4_KIND=1, max tokens/rank 4096 -> 2048, SGLANG_EXPERIMENTAL_ENABLE_PIECEWISE_CUDA_GRAPH_MOE_A2A=1, --enable-mixed-chunk, chunked-prefill 32768 -> 16384 with max-prefill-tokens 16384, --cuda-graph-max-bs 544, max-running-requests 4352, mem-fraction 0.835, SWA full-tokens ratio 0.12, SGLANG_OPT_USE_ONLINE_COMPRESS=1, SWA eviction/leaf-lock options, SGLANG_CLIP_MAX_NEW_TOKENS_ESTIMATION=8, NVSHMEM_DISABLE_IB=1; TP path gets cuda-graph-max-bs 512 and max-running 512 (was CONC*1.5); both paths --tokenizer-worker-num 8, --stream-interval 30, --enable-prefill-delayer; SWA full-tokens ratio 0.5 at 1k ISL vs 0.1 at 8k.
mechanism: MegaMoE fuses dispatch, expert GEMMs and combine into one DeepGEMM kernel, and FP4 activations halve its input bytes and use FP4 tensor cores; graphs that cover the MoE all-to-all remove launch gaps; mixed chunks put prefill and decode in one step; a larger SWA full-token pool for 1k prompts (whose sliding-window share is larger) avoids evictions; clipping max-new-token estimation admits more requests; more tokenizer workers and a coarser stream interval cut CPU overhead.
why: Most of the gain is a bundle of undocumented SGLANG_OPT_* and experimental environment switches plus a new all-to-all backend, each valid only in this nightly and several sub-1% alone, so a one-change, 1%-gate loop would reject many of them and could not know which exist. FP4 activations in the MoE are an accuracy trade. The SWA ratio and admission settings are tied to ISL and concurrency, so they encode workload knowledge across points.
evidence: +        --moe-a2a-backend megamoe ... +    export SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_USE_FP4_ACTS=1 ... +# 1k inputs need more SWA cache headroom than 8k inputs do. SWA_FULL_TOKENS_RATIO=0.5

The hang: with EP and moe_backend=auto the AITER MXFP4 backend was skipped and selection fell back to Mxfp4MoeBackend.EMULATION, which JIT-builds the Quark hw-emulation C++ extension on every worker; concurrent EP workers deadlocked on the shared torch_extensions build lock. Forcing aiter avoids the emulation path.
effect: Removes an ~8 hour startup hang on EP configs.
why: The flags are standard once the image has AITER MoE for M3. The hang diagnosis is the subtle part: a silent fallback to an emulation backend under EP only, visible as a timeout rather than an error, which a loop with a fixed time budget would record as a failed iteration and drop rather than explain.
evidence: +# with EP enabled and moe_backend=auto, the AITER MXFP4 backend is skipped and selection falls back to Mxfp4MoeBackend.EMULATION ... Concurrent EP workers deadlock on the shared torch_extensions build lock

what: MiniMax-M3 FP4 B300 vLLM: image from the vllm-minimax-m3-perf branch build to nightly-93d8f834; VLLM_FLASHINFER_ALLREDUCE_BACKEND=trtllm; --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90->0.95; --kv-cache-dtype fp8; search space reshaped from TP8/TP8-EP8/TP4-DEP4/TP8-DEP8 lanes to TP8 and TP4 only at c1-2, TP2 for c4-256, TP4 at c64, TP2 DEP2 at c512 (8k1k similar). Series with 949 (B200 twin).
mechanism: FlashInfer's TRT-LLM one-shot/two-shot allreduce (with fused residual+RMSNorm) is cheaper than the default custom allreduce at small TP; FP8 KV and higher memory fraction enlarge KV capacity so larger batches fit; small TP2 instances give more output tok/s per GPU for a model this size than TP8/EP8 except at the very lowest concurrency.
why: The env var and the fp8 KV flag are findable from vllm/envs.py and the CLI in a few iterations (if the pack does not fix KV dtype). The bulk of the per-GPU gain is the move to TP2 instances across most of the concurrency range, which is a parallelism change a pack usually fixes and whose value is only visible as tok/s/GPU across the whole Pareto sweep, not at one operating point.

what: DSR1 B200 FP4 SGLang MTP: image v0.5.12-cu130 -> v0.5.12.post1; TP8/EP1 c4-512 replaced by TP4/EP1 c1-32 and TP4/EP4 c64-256 (8k1k: TP4/EP4 with DP-attention); DP-attention path adds --data-parallel-size=TP --enable-dp-attention --enable-dp-attention-local-control-broadcast --enable-dp-lm-head --schedule-conservativeness 3.33 --enable-prefill-delayer, chunked-prefill 32768, scheduler-recv-interval 1; SGLANG_RADIX_FORCE_MISS=1 replaces --disable-radix-cache; drops --enable-symm-mem; explicit --disable-piecewise-cuda-graph; cuda-graph-max-bs 256, max-running-requests 256, mem-fraction-static 0.85, stream-interval 10. Series with 950 (non-MTP twin).
mechanism: Half-node TP4 instances double instances per node (better tok/s/GPU); at high concurrency DP-attention removes MLA KV replication and attention allreduce, and the DP-specific scheduler knobs (prefill delayer to align prefills across DP ranks, conservative admission to avoid KV retraction, local-control broadcast, DP LM head) keep ranks balanced; MTP adds speculative tokens at low latency.
why: The enabling move is topology: TP8 -> TP4 and DP-attention+EP4 at c>=64, which a pack fixing TP/EP and one concurrency cannot make. The supporting knobs (--enable-prefill-delayer, --schedule-conservativeness 3.33, --scheduler-recv-interval 1, local-control broadcast, DP LM head) only pay once DP-attention is on and mostly at high concurrency, so tried one at a time on the TP8 baseline each would read as noise or fail outright. The split of lanes by concurrency is a Pareto-front decision invisible from one operating point.

what: MiniMax-M3 MXFP8 MI355X vLLM EAGLE3: adds "attention_backend": "TRITON_ATTN" to --speculative-config so the drafter does not fall back to a slow default backend (the global --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN does not reach the draft model). Follows 973.
mechanism: The EAGLE3 drafter (a dense Llama MHA head) runs its own attention backend selection; without the override it picks a slow default, so every speculative step pays a slow draft forward. Pinning it to Triton keeps acceptance unchanged and shortens the draft forward.
effect: Throughput gains at 8k1k on MI355X TP4, growing with concurrency; acceptance unchanged (numbers not given).
why: The recipe's own earlier comment asserted the drafter needed no override because the server ran TRITON_ATTN globally; the fact that the global flag does not propagate to the draft model is a config-inheritance quirk. what: New GLM-5.1-FP8 GB200 Dynamo-SGLang disaggregated benchmark (lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.12, 14 topologies, 1k1k and 8k1k): prefill TP8/DP8 DP-attention (EP1) across two 4-GPU nodes, decode wide-EP DEP16/DEP32 with --moe-a2a-backend deepep (low_latency, SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=512), moe-runner deep_gemm, static EP dispatch, nsa trtllm backends, fp8 KV, NIXL transfer, multiple Dynamo frontends; low-latency lanes use per-node TP8 decode.
mechanism: Disaggregation isolates decode from prefill interference; wide-EP decode across 16-32 GPUs over MNNVL shrinks per-GPU expert weight so huge decode batches (1024 running) fit, with DeepEP low-latency all-to-all.
why: Every lever here (prefill/decode split, DEP32 decode over eight GB200 nodes, DeepEP all-to-all sizing, prefill:decode worker ratios) needs several nodes and an inter-node fabric; a one-node loop cannot run any of these topologies, let alone compare ratios.
evidence: decode: tensor-parallel-size: 32 / expert-parallel-size: 32 / moe-a2a-backend: deepep / deepep-mode: low_latency

what: New GLM-5.1 NVFP4 GB200 Dynamo-SGLang disagg MTP config (lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.13.post1-cu130), 8k1k and 1k1k, high-throughput and low-latency topologies: prefill DP-attention with flashinfer_trtllm MoE, flashinfer_cutlass FP4 GEMM, allreduce fusion; decode EAGLE (steps 2, topk 1, draft 3); SGLANG_MOE_NVFP4_DISPATCH=1 and DeepEP dispatch tokens 512 on decode.

why: The recipe is a set of multi-node prefill/decode topologies with worker ratios and wide-EP decode; none of it can be run or compared on one node. NVFP4 dispatch only matters when the all-to-all crosses many GPUs.

what: MiniMax-M3 MXFP8 MI300X vLLM: image minimax-m3 -> nightly-4559c43a; VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 (master switch was unset, so GEMMs and fused MoE ran on generic kernels) with VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MHA=0 (no calibrated FP8 attention scales; attention stays TRITON_ATTN); TORCH_BLAS_PREFER_HIPBLASLT=1, NCCL_MIN_NCHANNELS=112, GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=2; --async-scheduling; --max-num-batched-tokens 16384; TP8/EP8 rows replaced with TP8/EP1 (EP8 gave garbage output and 434 vs 905 tok/s/GPU at conc256).
mechanism: AITER kernels for decode GEMMs and fused MoE; more RCCL channels for TP8 allreduce; async scheduling overlaps CPU input prep with GPU decode; a larger prefill budget amortizes the per-step read of BF16-emulated MoE weights (~95 GB/rank) over more prompt tokens; EP1 avoids the broken and slower EP8 path.
effect: Total tok/s/GPU 1k1k: conc256 782.7->905, conc128 +4.9%, conc64 +17.5%, conc32 +10.8%, conc16 +6.6%, conc8 +7.1%, conc4 +5.6%; conc1-2 unchanged; GSM8K 0.959 held.

The one non-obvious part, keeping AITER MHA off because the checkpoint lacks FP8 attention scales, would surface as an accuracy failure the agent can read.

what: DSR1 B200 FP4 Dynamo-SGLang MTP disagg: prunes 8k1k low-latency points (1p5d c4-32, 1p3d c32-64, 1p1d c32); adds high-throughput 1p1d and 4p1d (DEP4 prefill / DEP8 decode) at conc 512 and a 4p1d c2048 point with its own engine tune: max-running-requests 2048 (avoid admission throttle), decode scheduler-recv-interval 1, prefill/decode stream-interval 100/34, SGLANG_HACK_SEQ_BOOTSTRAP_ROOM=1; restores 1k1k MTP recipes deleted in 953.

why: The new points are 4P1D DEP4/DEP8 disaggregated topologies over several B200 nodes; the c2048 tune only matters at that multi-node operating point and cannot be found or measured on one node.

what: New GLM-5.1-FP8 GB300 Dynamo-SGLang disagg MTP benchmark (v0.5.11-cu130), 11 topologies: prefill TP4 DP-attention + decode wide-EP DEP16/24/32/40 (8k1k) and DEP48/56 (1k1k) with DeepEP low_latency, 32 redundant experts, static dispatch, SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=1024 (must be >= ceil(cuda_graph_max_bs/dp_size)); per-node TP4 low-latency; EAGLE 2/1/3.
mechanism: Very wide EP decode (up to 56 GPUs) spreads experts so huge batches fit; redundant experts balance load; MTP reduces per-token latency.
why: Decode groups of 16-56 GPUs and prefill:decode ratios exist only across many GB300 nodes. The DeepEP buffer sizing rule (dispatch tokens per rank vs cuda-graph batch / DP size) appears only when DP is that wide.

what: DSV4 FP4 B200/B300 SGLang agentic (HiCache): image v0.5.13-cu130 -> nightly-dev-cu13-20260707-b4155233; SGLANG_ENABLE_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE=1 unconditionally (was HiCache-only) and SGLANG_OPT_UNIFIED_CACHE_FREE_OUT_OF_WINDOW_SLOTS=1; drops the local-RAID model-path workaround in the B200 launcher.
mechanism: DSV4's sliding-window-attention layers keep a separate SWA KV pool; freeing slots that fall out of the window during chunked prefill relieves SWA pool pressure, so fewer prefix entries are evicted and the multi-turn prefix-cache hit rate recovers.
effect: Not quantified; PR says it restores prefix-cache hit rate on multi-turn agentic workloads.
why: The problem shows up as a lower prefix-cache hit rate and more recomputed prefill on long multi-turn traces, not as a slow kernel, so a kernel profile does not point at it; the agent has to reason about SWA pool accounting under chunked prefill. The fix is an allocator change that ships in a newer SGLang nightly behind an env flag the pinned image lacks.
evidence: +export SGLANG_OPT_UNIFIED_CACHE_FREE_OUT_OF_WINDOW_SLOTS=1 / 'free out-of-window SWA KV slots during chunked prefill, relieving SWA pool pressure and restoring prefix-cache hit rate'

DSV4 FP4 MI355X SGLang: image v0.5.13.post1-20260618 -> v0.5.14-rocm720-mi35x-20260706; removes 15 now-default SGLANG_OPT_*/AITER/multi-stream env overrides; on the DP-attention path adds SGLANG_SHARED_EXPERT_TP1=1, SGLANG_DP_SHARED_EXPERT_LOCAL=1, SGLANG_DP_USE_GATHERV=1, SGLANG_DP_USE_REDUCE_SCATTER=1, GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=5 and --enable-two-batch-overlap (replacing --prefill-delayer-max-delay-ms 5000); --cuda-graph-max-bs CONC; --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3. Series with 998 (MTP twin).
mechanism: Two-batch overlap splits each DP-attention batch into two micro-batches so one's MoE dispatch/combine overlaps the other's compute; running the shared expert locally at TP1 per DP rank avoids gathering tokens for it; reduce-scatter/gatherv replace allreduce for DP token exchange; more HW queues let the overlapped streams run concurrently on ROCm; FP8 KV doubles KV capacity.
why: Two-batch overlap, local shared experts and reduce-scatter only pay together on the DP-attention+EP topology at high concurrency, and TBO on ROCm needs GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES raised or the streams serialize: tried singly, each would likely sit under the 1% gate. The shared-expert and DP env vars are undocumented SGLang environ flags, and GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES is a HIP runtime knob outside the framework. The image bump also changed which SGLANG_OPT defaults are right, which the loop cannot do.

what: New DSV4 FP4 MI355X vLLM AgentX (agentic trace replay) recipe on nightly-09663abd: KV_OFFLOAD_BACKEND native / mooncake / lmcache; LMCache built from source with HIP (dev branch, pinned for a hybrid-KV scheduler ValueError fix) as an MP server (L1 DRAM = TOTAL_CPU_DRAM_GB/(8/TP), chunk 256, LRU, l1 read TTL 7200 s, lmcache_driven transfer mode, LMCACHE_BLOCKING_TIMEOUT_SECS=1200, mq_timeout 6000) via LMCacheMPConnector; VLLM_PREFIX_CACHE_RETENTION_INTERVAL=32768; DP-attention runs behind vllm-router 0.1.14 with consistent_hash session routing.

why: The value depends on the workload's prefix-reuse pattern across turns and idle gaps, which a kernel profile does not show; the agent would need the trace statistics. Standing up LMCache meant building it from source for HIP, running a separate server process, and pinning a branch to get past a vLLM hybrid-KV scheduler bug, which is a long-build, multi-component change. Session-affinity routing is a client/router choice outside the serving process.

what: MiniMax-M3 MXFP8 MI355X vLLM PD-disagg: image nightly-2afa3f7e; per-worker flags synced with single-node 972 (--moe-backend aiter, --linear-backend emulation, --max-num-batched-tokens 32768) plus VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 and VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT6; all workers TP4 (TP8 and TP4/EP dropped), tuning the prefill:decode worker ratio instead: 1k1k 1P1D c1-1024 + 1P2D c256-2048; 8k1k 1P1D c1-512 + 2P1D c128-512 (<=3 workers for the 3-node pool).

The per-worker flags were ported from single-node work, and INT6 quick-reduce quantizes the allreduce, an accuracy trade a pack would gate.

GLM-5.2 NVFP4 B300 SGLang agentic: HiCache DRAM KV offload on all points of both arms: --enable-hierarchical-cache with host/device token-capacity ratio 0.75 (not GB-based sizing), io-backend direct, mem-layout page_first_direct, write policy write_back. Follows 1035; 1040 then retunes the throughput arm.
mechanism: The 1M-context agentic corpus outgrows the HBM KV pool past conc 8 (TP8) / 64 (DP8): KV usage pinned at 1.0 and the radix hit rate fell from a ~0.97 ceiling to 0.04-0.06, so every turn re-prefilled its whole history. HiCache spills evicted prefixes to pinned host DRAM and restores them over C2C instead of recomputing.
effect: Restores prefix reuse past the knee (no throughput numbers given); ratio 2 and GB-based sizing OOM-killed 3 TB nodes, ratio 0.75 = ~1.0 TB pinned host pools.
why: The diagnosis needs workload-level metrics (radix hit rate against its theoretical ceiling, KV usage at 1.0) rather than a kernel profile. Sizing is a trap: for DSA/MLA models the device pool is replicated on all 8 ranks, so the obvious per-rank GB sizing or the DSv4 default ratio pins 2.7 TB of host memory and OOM-kills the node, and an iteration that kills the node teaches the loop only that the direction failed. Packs often fix KV_OFFLOADING as part of the workload.
evidence: 'gpu_kv_cache_usage pinned at 1.0 and the radix hit rate collapsed from a ~0.97 theoretical ceiling to 0.04-0.06' / +    DEFAULT_HICACHE_RATIO=0.75

what: MiniMax-M3 MXFP8 MI355X vLLM TP4: image bump to nightly-9e57de71 carrying AITER page-16 sparse paged attention (vllm#47287); quick all-reduce INT6->INT4 at all concurrencies; a concurrency gate MM3_HIGH_CONC_FASTPATH (on only for isl>=8192 && conc>=64) that sets VLLM_ROCM_SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=1, VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_CAST_BF16_TO_FP16=0, VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION_MIN_SIZE_KB=256 and --linear-backend emulation; otherwise native Triton MXFP8 linear and non-shuffled Triton attention. Explicitly does not use the #47269 indexer-skip hf-override (FLOP reduction disallowed). Follows #2003.
mechanism: AITER Gluon paged attention reads only the top-k selected 128-token sparse blocks through page-16 views of the page-128 cache (fp8 KV, one KV head per rank at TP4), a faster kernel for the same sparse computation that pays off only with long context and big batch. bf16 hipBLASLt (emulation backend: dequantized weights) beats the native MXFP8 Triton GEMM when the dense linears are compute-bound at high concurrency, while the native GEMM wins memory-bound at low concurrency. INT4 quick-reduce halves all-reduce bytes vs INT6.
effect: vs #2003: 8k1k tput/GPU +3.3% conc128, +2.5% conc256, +4.7% conc512; neutral elsewhere.
why: The main win (sparse PA) exists only in a newer nightly that merged vllm#47287, so in a fixed image the agent cannot reach it at all. The linear-backend choice is counterintuitive: 'emulation' (dequantize MXFP8 to bf16 and use hipBLASLt) sounds like a debugging fallback, and it wins only when the GEMMs are compute-bound, so an agent at a low-concurrency point would correctly reject it and one at conc 512 would keep it, but neither would produce the per-regime gate. The value of the recipe is the gate across operating points, which a one-point loop never sees.
evidence: +if [ "$MM3_HIGH_CONC_FASTPATH" = "1" ]; then export VLLM_ROCM_SHUFFLE_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=1 ... LINEAR_ARGS=(--linear-backend emulation); 'native Triton MXFP8 linear GEMM wins in the memory-bound low-concurrency regime, while --linear-backend emulation (bf16 hipBLASLT) wins in the compute-bound high-concurrency regime'

what: Kimi-K2.5 FP4 MI355X vLLM disagg: image v0.24.0 -> nightly-2afa3f7e; all prefill/decode workers TP8 -> TP4, EP8 -> EP1 (expert parallel off); P/D topology split by concurrency: 1P(TP4)/1D(TP4) for conc 1-4, 1P(TP4)/2D(TP4) for conc 8-512; per-worker flags synced with single-node recipe (--kv-cache-dtype fp8, --max-model-len 32768, --max-num-seqs 256, --max-num-batched-tokens 32768, VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4, HSA_NO_SCRATCH_RECLAIM=1, drop VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_PAGED_ATTN=0 and SILU_MUL=0 overrides, drop the PIECEWISE cudagraph pin for default FULL_AND_PIECEWISE); router image re-pinned (old tag garbage-collected); bad nodes g09,g14 excluded.
mechanism: TP4 gives the same decode tok/s as TP8 with half the GPUs, so tok/s/GPU rises; EP with mori all2all was 14-27% slower than dense TP for this MoE; two decode engines at high concurrency spread KV and batch load (single decode engine unstable in the tail); fp8 KV, INT4 quick-reduce and full cudagraphs cut memory traffic, all-reduce bytes and launch overhead.
effect: Stated only qualitatively: TP8 decode no better than TP4 on tok/s/GPU; EP 14-27% slower than dense in a single-node TP8 sweep.
why: The core changes are topology: the number of decode engines per concurrency band and the TP width of each multi-node worker. The loop runs on one node with a fixed TP size, so it can neither try 1P2D nor measure tok/s per GPU across worker counts. Syncing the single-node flags into the disagg workers is easy, but deciding that a second decode node is worth its GPUs only above conc 8 needs a sweep across concurrencies and node counts.
evidence: high conc (8..512) on 1P(TP4)/2D(TP4) so decode load/KV is spread across two decode engines; 'single-node TP8 sweep showed EP -14% to -27% slower than dense'; -  tp: 8 / +  tp: 4 / -  ep: 8 / +  ep: 1

what: DSv4-Pro FP4 MI355X SGLang disagg: decode --context-length now derived from models.yaml, falling back to prefill's, so decode and prefill reject over-length requests symmetrically; router for non-agentic runs gets --cb-timeout-duration-secs 15 --retry-max-retries 3 and random policy, plus an end-to-end router readiness canary (one real generation) before evals; prefill max_total_tokens 262144 -> 2097152; sweep retune: drop 2P1D DEP8 and 1P1D DEP8 conc 1024, add 1P1D DEP8 conc 256/512 and a 1P1D pure TP8 scenario conc 1-128.
mechanism: Asymmetric admission let decode accept requests that prefill rejected, so they waited forever for a KV transfer (the 8k1k conc-500 straggler tail that set the run's duration). Bigger max_total_tokens matches the model's real KV budget. Pure TP8 without DP-attention/EP is a better low-concurrency point.
effect: Removes eval 503s and the conc-500 straggler tail; no throughput numbers given.

Prefill-only TBO splits a prefill batch into two micro-batches so one's communication overlaps the other's compute; GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=5 gives HIP enough hardware queues to run the overlapping streams concurrently. Decode TBO would drop MTP's spec_decode_metadata, so only prefill TBO is MTP-safe. Knowing that decode-TBO silently drops speculative metadata while prefill-only TBO is safe, and that ROCm needs GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES raised for the overlap to materialize, is framework- and HIP-runtime-specific knowledge an agent would have to read out of ATOM's source and AMD docs.

mechanism: Self-drafting MTP emits several tokens per verify step, which matters most when decode is memory-bound (low concurrency on PCIe GPUs). In SGLang, mem-fraction-static bounds weights plus KV and Mamba pools, so a 4.05 GiB/rank draft head has to be paid for by raising it; Mamba state is preallocated per max-running-request, so shrinking that cap frees memory for the draft.

An agent seeing 'pools empty' errors would iterate in the wrong direction unless it knows SGLang's memory accounting for hybrid models; and packs that fix spec-decoding on or off forbid the change outright.
