mechanism: Speculation multiplies tokens per target step, but each step verifies 1+K positions: at K=7 the 8-wide verify loses to no speculation once the GPU saturates even at golden AL 3.84, while K=2 clears break-even at both ends. vLLM rounds capture sizes to multiples of (1+K), so sizes must be given in tokens or graphs cover only MAX_NUM_SEQS/3 sequences. The drafter's KV costs ~25% of GPU KV. Tail fusion fuses K3's latent-MoE tail.
effect: Real acceptance on the agentic corpus: AL 1.16-2.01 (13-41% position-1) vs 4.18 on short context, because the draft's native window is 32k (YaRN x32); with real verification throughput regressed 20-63% vs non-MTP at conc 4/8. Reported numbers use synthetic AL 2.51.
why: Draft length is a trade between acceptance and verify width that flips sign with GPU saturation, so a one-concurrency loop picks the K that suits its point, not the one that clears break-even everywhere. Two blind spots: vLLM's silent rounding of cudagraph sizes to multiples of (1+K) leaves most batches uncaptured without an error, and the draft head's real acceptance collapses beyond its 32k native window, which only shows if the agent reads per-position acceptance on the real long-context traces rather than the synthetic AL the harness pins. Knowing the upstream recipe needs an off-by-default fusion env var is outside-the-tree knowledge.
evidence: at K=7 the target verifies 8 positions per step, which loses to no-speculation once the GPU saturates even at the forced golden AL of 3.84 (K=2 clears break-even at both ends of the cost range ...). cudagraph capture consequently enumerates multiples of (1+2)=3, since vLLM rounds configured sizes to multiples of (1+N)

what: New Qwen3.5-397B NVFP4 GB300 SGLang AgentX recipes (sglang nightly-dev-cu13-20260724): aggregated TP4 on one 4-GPU tray at conc 1 and 96 with NEXTN MTP (3 steps, topk 1, 4 draft tokens), hierarchical KV cache to host DRAM (hicache, io-backend kernel, page_first_direct layout, dram-utilization 0.80), symm-mem, NVLS, trtllm_mha attention, flashinfer_trtllm MoE, chunked prefill 16384, mem-fraction 0.8; disaggregated 1P1D-4P1D (TP4/DEP4 prefill, TP4/DEP4/DEP8 decode, MTP on prefill too, mooncake KV transfer, X-Dynamo-Session-Id conv-aware routing) over 7 Pareto points at conc 32-384.
mechanism: MTP raises tokens per decode step; hicache keeps evicted agentic prefixes in host memory so later turns hit cache instead of re-prefilling; session-header routing pins a conversation to the worker holding its prefix; disaggregation separates long prefills from decode at high concurrency.
why: The aggregated half is reachable flag by flag on one node. The Pareto frontier itself is seven multi-node prefill/decode allocations with session-affinity routing, which needs several nodes, a router and a sweep across concurrencies. Hicache's value depends on the agentic working set exceeding GPU KV, which a per-kernel profile does not show.
evidence: agg: single aggregated node (TP4, MTP/NEXTN, hierarchical KV cache), concurrencies [1, 96]; disagg: 1P1D-4P1D (TP4/DEP4 prefill, TP4/DEP4/DEP8 decode, MTP/NEXTN, hicache, conv-aware routing) over 7 Pareto points at concurrency 32-384

what: New DSv4-Pro FP4 B300 Dynamo-SGLang STP 8k1k disagg (sglang nightly-dev-cu13-20260721): five recipes, one per band: 1P1D TP4/TP4 at conc 1-32; 1P1D DEP4 prefill/DEP8 decode at 256; 2P1D DEP4/DEP8 at 768; 4P1D DEP4/DEP8 at 2048; MoE a2a backend megamoe with DeepGEMM mega-MoE FP4 activations and MXF4 kind (SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK 8192 prefill / 1280 decode), dp-attention with dp-lm-head, moe-dense-tp-size 1, Nixl KV transfer, decode polling interval 8, mem-fraction 0.90/0.94, decode cuda-graph-max-bs 1280, 8 extra Dynamo frontends, KV router with overlap weight 0 and no KV events. mechanism: Each concurrency band gets its own prefill:decode ratio and parallelism: pure TP at low concurrency for latency, DEP with megamoe all-to-all at high concurrency so experts are spread and batched; more prefill workers per decode as concurrency rises; the per-rank token cap sizes the MoE dispatch buffers to the phase (large prefill chunks vs decode batch); extra frontends keep the HTTP layer from bottlenecking at conc 2048.
why: The recipe is a Pareto set of multi-node topologies (1P1D to 4P1D) chosen per concurrency band, which needs several nodes and a sweep the loop cannot run. The megamoe knobs (FP4 activations, MXF4 kind, max tokens per rank per phase) are undocumented SGLang/DeepGEMM environment variables whose right values differ between prefill and decode roles; an agent would have to find them in the source and could only test one role on one node.
evidence: +    SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK: "8192" (prefill) / "1280" (decode); +      moe-a2a-backend: "megamoe"; conc-list [256] 1P DEP4 / 1D DEP8; [2048] 4P DEP4 / 1D DEP8

what: MiniMax-M3 MXFP4 MI355X vLLM STP: image -> vllm-openai-rocm nightly-69715823; INT4 quick all-reduce (VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4, VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_CAST_BF16_TO_FP16=0, VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION_MIN_SIZE_KB=256); --kv-cache-dtype fp8; search space reduced to TP4 conc 1-512 (drop TP8, TP8/EP8, TP4/EP4, TP2/EP2, dp-attn); no indexer-skip hf-overrides (FLOP reduction disallowed). Same INT4 knob set reused in id 1073.
mechanism: The ~1.5 MB decode all-reduces are the largest decode kernel at high concurrency; INT4 quick-reduce cuts their bytes about 4x, but vLLM's default INT4 size gate for bf16 TP4 is 16 MB, so it only applies to decode tensors once the minimum size is lowered to 256 KB. fp8 KV halves KV reads.
effect: INT4 all-reduce: ~12-17% lower TPOT at conc 64/128/256 (closing the high-concurrency gap to ATOM).
why: The knob is documented, but enabling it alone is a no-op for decode because of a 16 MB default size gate; an agent that sets INT4, sees no change, and records a dead end would never reach the 12-17% unless it reads the quick-reduce dispatch code. Spotting that all-reduce is the biggest decode kernel is profile-visible, which is why this is medium rather than hard.
evidence: The MIN_SIZE_KB override is required: vLLM's default INT4 quick-reduce size gate for (bf16, TP4) is 16 MB, so it never fires for decode-sized tensors without it; measured ~-12% to -17% TPOT at conc 64/128/256

why: Two cross-point decisions: the draft-depth taper only appears when MTP's value is measured across concurrencies, and the 1P6D layout (six decode engines per prefill) is a multi-node allocation the loop cannot build. A one-point agent could tune depth for its own concurrency, but not produce the schedule or the topology.
evidence: +# EAGLE draft depth is tapered down as concurrency grows; conc-list [8, 32, 64] ... disagg-b300-1p6d-dep4-tp4-mtp.yaml (decode num-worker 6, tp 4)

Parallel tokenization keeps 256k-token warmups under the client timeout.
why: The hicache crossover concurrency differs by TP size and GPU memory, so the arm boundaries come from sweeping concurrency per TP, not from one operating point. Sizing hicache correctly requires knowing how SGLang allocates host pools for a hybrid Mamba model with a NEXTN draft (target, Mamba and 1/15 draft pools), which is source-level knowledge; getting it wrong over-commits host DRAM.

what: MiniMax-M3 MXFP4 MI355X vLLM disagg: image rocm/vllm-dev 0.23.1 mori -> vllm-openai-rocm nightly-2dfaae75 (AITER MoE with shared-expert fusion); VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1 on both roles; prefill workers only get VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 and VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_MAX_SIZE_BYTES_MB=2048 through a new prefill_env channel in server_vllm.sh; 1P1D TP4 sweep capped at conc 256; 2P1D TP4 layout dropped (CI-flaky, negligible curve impact).
mechanism: Prefill all-reduces at TP8 carry thousands of tokens per call (hundreds of MB), above quick-reduce's default maximum size, so raising the cap to 2048 MB lets INT4 quantized all-reduce cut their bytes ~4x; decode keeps full-precision all-reduce. Shared-expert fusion computes the shared expert inside the AITER fused-MoE launch.
why: Quick-reduce has hidden size gates at both ends: decode needs the minimum lowered (ids 1089, 1073), prefill needs the maximum raised, and setting INT4 alone silently does nothing on prefill-sized tensors. Applying it to one role only requires the disaggregated deployment the loop does not have, and knowing that the size cap exists means reading the ROCm quick-reduce dispatch code.

Same PR as id 1147.
mechanism: Weighted-random picking spreads requests across workers instead of piling onto the top-scored one under high concurrency. Randomized DP dummy inputs make idle DP ranks' padding batches route to varied experts instead of all hitting the same ones, so the expert-parallel all-to-all is not skewed by dummy tokens. Bounding prefill to 16 sequences x 32k tokens and max-model-len to the 8k1k need frees KV and activation memory; NVSHMEM fabric handles replace NCCL symmetric memory for the MNNVL all-to-all.

what: Kimi-K3 FP4 B300 vLLM AgentX moved to TP8 x DCP8 (--decode-context-parallel-size 8 --dcp-comm-backend a2a, VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_A2A/Q_GATHER/KV_GATHER=1), TOKENSPEED_MLA attention for target and draft, VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1, Mooncake as the external KV tier (replacing SimpleCPU), on an image built from vLLM's agentx-k3 branch (5894fdf: K3 DCP, DSpark under DCP, Mooncake hybrid). Concurrency selects the drafting level: DSpark K=7 (golden AL 3.84) at conc<=8, K=3 (AL 3.00) at conc 16, no drafting above 16; sweep extended to conc 1-70. Capture sizes in steps of 1+K. Follows ids 1155 (B300 DSpark refresh); the previous header noted that K=7 verify loses to no speculation once the GPU saturates.
mechanism: MLA keeps one latent KV head, so plain TP8 replicates the whole KV cache on every rank; DCP8 shards decode KV across the 8 ranks, giving about 8x KV capacity and letting the GPU-resident tier hold many more long agentic sessions (the old recipe could not finish warmup at c16). Speculation depth shrinks as concurrency grows because verify width is real compute once the GPU is saturated.
effect: Not stated; the sweep now reaches conc 70 where the previous resident arm stalled at c16.
why: DCP for this model exists only in a branch image (agentx-k3 @ 5894fdf) carrying DCP, DSpark-under-DCP and Mooncake-hybrid changes; in the fixed image the flag is not usable. Seeing that the capacity wall is caused by MLA KV replication across TP ranks needs reasoning about memory layout across ranks, not a kernel profile. The concurrency-gated spec depth is a policy across operating points; at one concurrency the loop would pick one K and never write the gate.
evidence: # The image carries the Kimi-K3 DCP, DSpark-under-DCP and Mooncake-hybrid changes (vllm-project/vllm agentx-k3 @ 5894fdf); CP_ARGS+=(--decode-context-parallel-size "$DCP_SIZE" --dcp-comm-backend a2a); conc <= 8 DSpark level 7 ... conc > 16 no drafting

what: GLM-5.2 FP4 B300 SGLang AgentX MTP: HiCache host pool sized absolutely with --hicache-size 270 (GB per rank for the target KV pool; capped at 270) instead of --hicache-ratio 0.75 (~128 GB/rank). Measured footprint 270 + 61.88 (DSA indexer) + 3.46 (MTP draft) = 335.34 GB/rank, 2.683 TB across TP8. Same idea applied per concurrency on B200 in id 1204.
mechanism: A larger host KV tier holds more of the agentic sessions' prefixes, so fewer turns re-prefill; an absolute size keeps the host capacity fixed when the HBM pool changes.
why: The knob is documented, but the safe value is a whole-node memory budget: earlier GB-based sizing pinned the whole DRAM budget and OOM-killed the node, and the indexer and draft pools silently inherit the target pool's slot count with their own bytes per token. Finding 270 GB needs measuring host-memory use across pools and knowing the node's headroom, and the benefit appears only at concurrencies whose working set overflows the smaller pool.

mechanism: Under speculative decoding with DP attention SGLang synchronizes decode across ranks, so a rank with nothing to prefill runs idle batches while the busiest rank sets the step time; bounding the decode run to 20 steps before admitting prefill rebalances ranks. Capturing graphs up to the real batch sizes keeps fan-out bursts out of eager mode. Concurrency-scaled memory fractions avoid single-rank OOMs that would hang the engine.
effect: --prefill-decode-interval 20: +28% output throughput at conc 128 (2,433-2,470 -> 3,127-3,161 tok/s), gap to vLLM 1.32x -> 1.03x; TTFT p50 2.2x and p90 3.3x worse; at c256 with CPU tier SGLang 4,168 vs vLLM 4,199 tok/s.

The memory-fraction schedule comes from OOMs on a single DP rank that silently hang the engine at specific concurrencies; a one-point loop sees either a hang or a pass, never the schedule. The prefill-delayer trades a 2.2-3.3x TTFT regression for throughput, which a gate that watches latency would reject and a throughput gate would keep, so whether the agent keeps it depends on what its gate measures.

what: Kimi-K3 FP4 MI355X ATOM AgentX DSpark retune (follows id 1214) on image kimi_k3_agentic_0821, points [1,4,8,10] -> [1,2,4,8,12,16,32,40,56], every point retuned: decode-context-parallel-size 8 from c8 up (off at c1-4); DSpark K=7 (AL 3.84) at c1-4, K=3 (AL 3.00) at c8-16, no drafting from c32; per-concurrency max-num-seqs (32/24/64/80/72), batched tokens 8192 or 4096, memory 0.86-0.88, ReplaySSM on with 96 in-GPU state checkpoint slots only at c8/12, CPU state-offload tier (32 GB/rank) from c16; LMCache paged-KV tier halved to 96-100 GB/rank because pinning 200 GB per rank took ranks more than 600 s apart and tripped PyTorch's hardcoded NCCL process-group timeout; LMCACHE_CHUNK_SIZE 1024 (page 128 x dcp 8) so offload hash blocks align under DCP; OFFLOAD_GPU_STAGING_CHUNKS 32; keeps INT4 quick-reduce, SITUV2 A4W4, FlyDSL stage-2 FP8, ptpc_fp8 online quant, fp8 KV.
mechanism: At 100K+ token contexts decode is KV-bandwidth-bound, so sharding the KV read over 8 GPUs with DCP speeds each step once there is enough load to amortize the extra collectives; speculation depth falls as concurrency rises because verify compute stops being free; the recurrent-state handling (GPU checkpoints with ReplaySSM vs CPU state tier) is chosen per band by where HBM runs out.
effect: Not stated; measured CPU-tier hit rate 0.0% at c8/12 and 0.3-2.4% above, so halving the tier cost little.
why: The recipe is a per-concurrency policy over DCP, draft depth, ReplaySSM and the state tier; a loop at one concurrency can tune one row but would never produce the table, and DCP is a parallelism change a TP-fixed pack may forbid. Two settings come from failures that hide their cause: the NCCL 600 s timeout appears only when ranks pin large host pools at different speeds and kills workers before serving, and a chunk size that does not equal block size times DCP silently misaligns offload hashes so the tier never hits. It also depends on a newer purpose-built ATOM image.
evidence: 'Shard the decode KV read across all 8 GPUs with decode-context-parallel-size 8 from concurrency 8 up'; 'the eight ranks finished pinning more than 600 seconds apart, which is exactly PyTorch's hardcoded NCCL process-group timeout'; 'Set LMCACHE_CHUNK_SIZE to 1024 ... with decode context parallelism the offload hash block is block-size times dcp'
